## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Performance

Assesses performance risks that are visible in code and configuration: caching, blocking I/O, client and connection
reuse, N+1 and chatty data access, extraneous fetching, offloading of heavy work, hot-path efficiency and scale-out
readiness. It uses a local, pinned summary of Azure Well-Architected Performance Efficiency and Azure Architecture
Center guidance. Runtime measurement, load testing and profiling are out of scope.

#### Inputs

Data-access code (repositories, ORM queries, SQL, schema migrations), request handlers, client and DI/startup
registration, caching code and config, background-job code, web-server config, and hosting/scaling config, per
`compliance-inventory`.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/azure-performance-efficiency.md` — AZPE-01…AZPE-53. Always load.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md`, `references/performance-config-signals.md`, the
   standards file and, for each language id in `01-inventory.json`, `references/languages/<id>.md` if it exists.
2. Concurrency model: classify each request-handling stack as async-first or thread-per-request using the language
   files. On thread-per-request stacks skip AZPE-13 and AZPE-15 ("thread-per-request stack; synchronous I/O is the
   model"). AZPE-14 and AZPE-18 apply to both. On async-first stacks, a blocking I/O call in a request path fails
   AZPE-13 with confidence `high` when the async alternative is used elsewhere in the codebase, otherwise `medium`.
3. Hot paths: count loop, query and allocation patterns (PERF-04, PERF-05) only in request, message, batch or
   scheduled-job paths that iterate over data that isn't evidently small and fixed (a result set, a collection from
   input, a page of records). Exclude startup code, scripts, migrations, tests and loops over constants. Use
   confidence `medium` unless the data is evidently unbounded (e.g. `findAll()`, `objects.all()`).
4. Multi-instance: apply AZPE-07 only when the files show more than one instance can run (replicas,
   autoscale, instance count, Kubernetes Deployment/HPA, serverless; see `performance-config-signals.md`).
   Otherwise skip ("no multi-instance evidence in scope").
5. Config in scope: judge AZPE-49…AZPE-51 only when hosting, ingress, autoscale or server config is in the files;
   otherwise skip ("no hosting/scaling config in scope"), which is never a failure. If PERF-08 then has no applicable
   element, mark it N/A.
6. Boundaries: don't fail for retries, backoff, timeouts or general circuit breakers (review-reliability; AZPE-06
   judges only cache fallback); API caching headers, pagination contract, long-running-operation shape or rate-limit
   responses (review-api-design; skip AZPE-11 for HTTP APIs with reason "API caching headers judged by
   review-api-design"); instrumentation, cache hit/miss metrics or telemetry volume (review-observability);
   performance alerts (review-monitoring); autoscale maximum bounds, over-provisioning or data archive/purge
   (review-cost-sustainability); cache authentication, TLS or access control (security skills; AZPE-12 judges only
   key scoping and sensitive data in shared caches); statelessness, session state and sticky sessions
   (review-twelve-factor TF-06); load and performance tests (review-testing TST-12). Never recommend caching
   authenticated, per-user or sensitive responses (`no-store`: review-security-web-api SEC-WA-08).
7. For each check (PERF-01…PERF-08), evaluate only the elements it lists whose "Applies when" condition holds. If
   none apply, mark the check N/A with that reason.
8. Evidence rule: fail only on concrete evidence in the files (see the language files' fail signals, e.g.
   `new HttpClient()` inside an action method, `.Result` on an EF Core call in a controller, `requests.get` inside
   `async def`, a loop that calls `repository.GetById`, `ToList()` before `Where`, `IMemoryCache.Set` with no
   expiration, `clientAffinityEnabled: true`). Use confidence `medium` unless the evidence is unambiguous.
9. Severity: every Finding takes the check's default severity from `checklist.md`;
   `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is always that default.
10. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `AZPE-01`); the report script derives `standard` and
    `url` from it, so don't write them. Never cite the language or config-signals files.

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

## File: `references/checklist.md`

### Checklist — Performance

Subject: Performance

Each check is evaluated against the local standards elements it lists (see `standards/`). Every element belongs to exactly one check.
Source: AZPE = `standards/azure-performance-efficiency.md`.

| id | Sub-subject | Check | Default severity | Elements | Source |
|----|-------------|-------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| PERF-01 | Performance | Expensive or repeated reads are cached with bounded size, expiry matched to volatility, invalidation on write, graceful fallback, and multi-instance-safe, user-scoped keys | Warning | AZPE-01–AZPE-12 | AZPE |
| PERF-02 | Performance | I/O in request paths doesn't block: async APIs on async-first stacks, no blocking on async results, independent calls concurrent, and fan-out bounded | Warning | AZPE-13–AZPE-18 | AZPE |
| PERF-03 | Performance | Shareable clients (HTTP, messaging, DB/SDK, cache) and expensive objects are created once and reused; connections are pooled, released promptly and sized explicitly | Warning | AZPE-19–AZPE-24 | AZPE |
| PERF-04 | Performance | No N+1 query patterns or chatty I/O: related data loaded eagerly or in batches, writes batched, coarse-grained remote calls, buffered file I/O, bounded batches | Warning | AZPE-25–AZPE-29 | AZPE |
| PERF-05 | Performance | No repeated expensive work in hot paths: invariants hoisted, fitting data structures, low allocation, memoized computations, limited logging in loops | Information | AZPE-30–AZPE-34 | AZPE |
| PERF-06 | Performance | Data retrieval is efficient: projection, filtering and aggregation in the store, bounded queries, no business logic in the DB, separate stores for logs and queues, indexes, optimistic concurrency | Warning | AZPE-35–AZPE-41 | AZPE |
| PERF-07 | Performance | Long-running and resource-intensive work is offloaded from request paths to managed, independently scaled workers, scheduled or prioritized appropriately | Warning | AZPE-42–AZPE-46 | AZPE |
| PERF-08 | Performance | The app is ready to scale out and serves efficiently: sound autoscale triggers, resource limits, compression/HTTP/2, CDN for static content, no singleton bottleneck (statelessness and sticky sessions: review-twelve-factor TF-06) | Information | AZPE-49–AZPE-53 | AZPE |

Totals: 53 AZPE elements across 8 checks.

Retries, timeouts and circuit breakers are reviewed by `review-reliability`; the HTTP API contract (caching headers, pagination, long-running operations) by `review-api-design`; instrumentation and telemetry volume by `review-observability`.

## File: `references/performance-config-signals.md`

### Performance config signals

Local lookup table, not a standard. Use it for the multi-instance rule (`SKILL.md` step 4), the config-in-scope rule
(step 5) and PERF-07 / PERF-08 evidence; cite the AZPE elements, never this file. If a hosting or scaling setting isn't
listed, apply the closest row only when it clearly fits; otherwise add
`localized-standard-gap: unrecognized config <setting>` to `notes`.

"Hosting/scaling config in scope" means at least one file in the subject's list matches a cell in the Session
affinity, Autoscale triggers, Resource limits or Compression / HTTP/2 rows.

| Signal | Azure (Bicep / ARM / Terraform `azurerm`) | AWS | GCP | Kubernetes / ingress | App / server config |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-instance evidence (step 4) | App Service plan `capacity` / `sku.capacity` > 1; `Microsoft.Insights/autoscalesettings` / `azurerm_monitor_autoscale_setting`; Container Apps `minReplicas` > 1 or `maxReplicas` > 1; Functions Consumption / Flex / Premium plans | ECS `desired_count` > 1; Auto Scaling group; `aws_appautoscaling_*`; Lambda | Cloud Run `max_instance_count` > 1; managed instance group autoscaler; Cloud Functions | `Deployment` `spec.replicas` > 1; `HorizontalPodAutoscaler`; KEDA `ScaledObject` | gunicorn / uWSGI with several worker processes (process-local caches and sessions aren't shared) |
| Session affinity (scope detection only; affinity is judged by review-twelve-factor TF-06) | App Service `clientAffinityEnabled: true`; Application Gateway `cookieBasedAffinity: 'Enabled'`; Front Door `sessionAffinityState: 'Enabled'` | ALB / ELB target group `stickiness` enabled | backend service `session_affinity` other than `NONE` | Service `sessionAffinity: ClientIP`; ingress-nginx annotation `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/affinity: cookie` | — |
| Autoscale triggers (AZPE-44, AZPE-49) | autoscale profile `rules` (`metricTrigger` threshold, `scaleAction` cooldown), `capacity.minimum`; Container Apps `scale.rules` (HTTP, queue, custom) | target-tracking / step scaling policies; SQS-depth-based scaling | autoscaler `cpu_utilization`, `load_balancing_utilization`; Cloud Run `max_instance_request_concurrency`, `min_instance_count` | HPA `metrics`, `minReplicas`, `behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds`; KEDA queue scalers | — |
| Resource limits (AZPE-50) | Container Apps `resources.cpu` / `memory`; AKS pod specs (see Kubernetes) | ECS task definition `cpu` / `memory` | Cloud Run `resources.limits` | `resources.requests` / `resources.limits` on containers; `LimitRange` | JVM `-Xmx` / `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage`; .NET `GCHeapHardLimit` / `DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit` |
| Compression / HTTP/2 (AZPE-51) | App Service `siteConfig.http20Enabled`; Front Door route `compressionSettings` / `isCompressionEnabled` | CloudFront `compress = true`; ALB HTTP/2 (on by default) | HTTPS load balancer HTTP/2 | ingress-nginx ConfigMap `use-gzip`, `use-http2` | `AddResponseCompression`; `server.compression.enabled`, `server.http2.enabled`; Django `GZipMiddleware`; nginx `gzip on`, `listen … http2` |
| CDN / static hosting (AZPE-52) | Front Door / CDN profiles; Static Web Apps; storage static website | CloudFront + S3 | Cloud CDN; Firebase Hosting | — | static files served by the app framework with no cache headers or CDN in front (fail signal when assets are significant) |
| Queue workers (AZPE-44, AZPE-53) | Container Apps / Functions with queue scale rules; WebJobs | ECS services or Lambdas triggered by SQS | Cloud Run jobs / Pub/Sub push subscribers | separate `Deployment` for workers; KEDA `ScaledObject` on queue length | a worker pinned to one instance (`replicas: 1` / `maxReplicas: 1`) consuming all of a queue's load is a fail signal for AZPE-53 |

## File: `references/standards/azure-performance-efficiency.md`

*Load rule: AZPE-01…AZPE-53. Always load.*

### Azure performance efficiency guidance — localized summary

- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (the pages use no normative keywords); severity is the owning check's default.
- Every element is Scope G (generic). No element depends on Azure services. Azure product names in the sources (Azure Managed Redis, Service Bus) are generalized to "distributed cache", "message queue".

`pe-check` (PE:01–PE:12) and `ap` (antipattern catalog) are traceability and drift only; no element cites them.

#### PERF-01 — Caching of expensive or repeated reads

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| AZPE-01 | Data that's read often and changes rarely, or is expensive to fetch (reference data, repeated query results, remote lookups), is cached instead of fetched from the source on every request. | repeated reads of the same data in request paths |
| AZPE-02 | Cached entries expire. An absolute or sliding TTL is set per cache or per entry and matches the data's volatility and the staleness callers can accept. Data that must be current bypasses the cache. | cache present |
| AZPE-03 | Caches are bounded. In-process caches have a size limit or eviction policy. Caches without built-in expiry are swept so they can't grow without limit. | in-process cache |
| AZPE-04 | Writes keep the cache consistent: the source is updated and the entry invalidated (cache-aside), or both are updated in one write (write-through) where read-after-write freshness is needed. | app writes data it also caches |
| AZPE-05 | The cache is not the system of record: important changes are persisted to the data store, not held only in the cache. | app writes to the cache |
| AZPE-06 | If the cache is unavailable, the request doesn't fail: the app falls back to the source and protects it from a sudden surge. General circuit breakers belong to reliability. | shared/distributed cache |
| AZPE-07 | With several instances, mutable shared data isn't kept only in per-instance memory caches: a shared cache is used, or private caches use short expiry (or a local + shared two-level cache). | multi-instance rule + in-process cache of mutable data |
| AZPE-08 | Concurrent updates to shared cached values use atomic operations or optimistic concurrency, not a separate read-then-write. | shared cache updated by several instances |
| AZPE-09 | Reads and writes of several cache keys are batched (multi-get/multi-set, pipelining), not one round trip per key in a loop. | several keys per operation |
| AZPE-10 | Static reference data that fits in the cache is primed at startup; very large seeding that would overload the source at startup is avoided. | reference data cached |
| AZPE-11 | Cacheable web pages and static assets send caching headers (Cache-Control/ETag), and static asset URIs are versioned so clients pick up changes. HTTP APIs: skipped (review-api-design). Never recommend caching authenticated, per-user or sensitive responses (`no-store`: review-security-web-api SEC-WA-08). | web app serving pages or static assets |
| AZPE-12 | User- or tenant-specific data in a shared cache uses keys that include the user/tenant scope. Sensitive data is read from the primary source, not cached in a shared cache. | shared cache holding per-user data |

#### PERF-02 — Non-blocking I/O in request paths

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| AZPE-13 | On async-first stacks, I/O in request paths (DB, HTTP, queue, storage, file) uses the library's async API where one exists. Short, low-contention local I/O (e.g. small files read at startup) is exempt. | async-first stack |
| AZPE-14 | Async operations aren't blocked on synchronously in request or handler code (waiting on a task, future or promise result); one blocking call blocks the whole call chain. | any stack using async APIs |
| AZPE-15 | Synchronous I/O isn't wrapped in a thread-offload "async" wrapper as a fix in server code; a native async API is used, because wrappers add threads and overhead. | async-first stack |
| AZPE-16 | Service interfaces and client libraries that the repo exposes offer async versions of I/O-bound operations, so callers can stay non-blocking. | repo exposes an I/O-bound service or client library |
| AZPE-17 | Independent I/O calls in one operation run concurrently (e.g. awaited together) rather than one after another, when order doesn't matter. | ≥ 2 independent remote calls in one handler |
| AZPE-18 | Concurrency against shared resources is bounded (semaphore, bounded executor or parallelism, pool size), so unblocked work doesn't starve or throttle downstream resources. | parallel or concurrent fan-out |

#### PERF-03 — Client, connection and expensive-object reuse

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| AZPE-19 | Shareable, thread-safe broker clients (HTTP, messaging, database/document SDK, cache connection) are created once and reused for the app's lifetime (singleton, DI or factory), not per request or call. | such clients used |
| AZPE-20 | Long-lived HTTP clients also handle connection lifetime and DNS changes, through a client factory or a pooled-connection lifetime setting. | long-lived HTTP client |
| AZPE-21 | Per-request settings (e.g. default headers) aren't changed on shared client instances; they're set once at startup or put on the individual request. | shared clients |
| AZPE-22 | Database connections come from a pool and are released promptly after each unit of work; scarce connections aren't held open across requests or idle periods. | DB access |
| AZPE-23 | Pool sizes are set explicitly for the concurrency each instance must support and stay within the service's connection limits. Defaults that run out under load are avoided, and pooling isn't disabled. | pool config present, or high-concurrency service |
| AZPE-24 | Objects that are expensive to create are reused (pooling, or lazy creation of one shared instance) instead of being created and destroyed repeatedly. | expensive objects in hot paths |

#### PERF-04 — N+1 and chatty I/O

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| AZPE-25 | Related data is loaded with joins, eager loading or batch fetching, not one query per item while iterating a result set (including lazy-loaded navigation used in loops or during serialization). | ORM or data-access code |
| AZPE-26 | Multiple records are written with batch or bulk operations, or committed in one unit of work, not one round trip per record in a loop. | writes in loops |
| AZPE-27 | One logical operation isn't split into many small remote calls (one per property or item); coarse-grained or batch endpoints are used or offered. | remote API calls |
| AZPE-28 | File and stream writes are buffered into larger operations, not repeated open/write/close cycles for small pieces. | file I/O in loops |
| AZPE-29 | Combined requests stay bounded: a batch fetches only what the caller is likely to use, and write batches are size-limited. | batching present |

#### PERF-05 — Efficient hot-path code

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| AZPE-30 | Calls, lookups and computations that don't change inside a loop are moved out of it; redundant calculations and repeated validations on the same path are removed. | hot-path rule |
| AZPE-31 | Data structures fit the access pattern (e.g. a hash lookup instead of repeated linear searches inside a loop). | lookups in loops |
| AZPE-32 | Allocations in hot paths are kept low: no repeated string concatenation in loops, buffers reused, large objects pooled, objects created lazily. | hot-path rule |
| AZPE-33 | Results of expensive, repeatable computations are reused (memoized or cached) instead of recomputed on every call. | repeated pure computation |
| AZPE-34 | Logging and diagnostics inside hot loops are limited (no per-iteration info-level logging), and debug-only features (e.g. remote debugging) are off in production config. Telemetry volume: OBS-10. | hot loops with logging |

#### PERF-06 — Efficient data retrieval and data-store use

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| AZPE-35 | Queries select only the columns or fields they need (projection), not whole entities or `SELECT *` trimmed afterwards in code. | data access |
| AZPE-36 | Filtering, sorting and aggregation run in the data store, not after rows are loaded into memory (e.g. a query materialized before its filter, or an expression the ORM can't translate that forces client-side evaluation). | data access |
| AZPE-37 | Queries that could return unbounded results are paged or capped with a server-side maximum (record count or query time limit). Data layer only; the API pagination contract is api-design's. | list/search/export reads |
| AZPE-38 | The database isn't used as an application engine: formatting, string manipulation and complex business logic aren't pushed into stored procedures, triggers or queries. Aggregation stays in the database. | stored procedures or SQL in the repo |
| AZPE-39 | Data with different access patterns uses separate stores; logs, telemetry and queue messages aren't written to the business transactional database. | app writes logs or queues to the business DB |
| AZPE-40 | Columns used often in WHERE, JOIN and ORDER BY are indexed in the schema or migrations; low-cardinality and redundant indexes are avoided. | schema or migration files in scope |
| AZPE-41 | Restrictive locking is avoided (no unnecessary lock hints or long pessimistic locks); concurrent updates use optimistic concurrency (version column, rowversion, ETag). | update paths |

#### PERF-07 — Long-running and resource-intensive work is offloaded

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| AZPE-42 | CPU- or I/O-intensive or long-running work started by a request goes to a queue and a separate worker (queue-based load leveling), and the request returns promptly. The 202/status contract is api-design's. | such work in request handlers |
| AZPE-43 | Request handlers don't start unmanaged threads or fire-and-forget tasks for heavy work; background work runs in managed hosted services or workers. | web front end |
| AZPE-44 | Background workers scale independently of the front end (competing consumers; autoscaling on queue length when IaC is in scope). | queue workers present |
| AZPE-45 | Heavy work that isn't time-sensitive is scheduled off-peak or rate-limited, so it doesn't use capacity that time-sensitive flows need. | batch or scheduled jobs |
| AZPE-46 | Where flows or tenants have different priorities, critical work is prioritized (priority queues, rate limits on non-critical callers or tenants). | several flows or tenants share a queue or API |

#### PERF-08 — Scale-out readiness and efficient serving

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| AZPE-47 | (retired 2026-11-09; owned by review-twelve-factor TF-06) App instances are stateless: session and user state lives in an external shared store, not in process memory or on local disk. | — |
| AZPE-48 | (retired 2026-11-09; owned by review-twelve-factor TF-06) Client/session affinity (sticky sessions) is off unless justified in the files. | — |
| AZPE-49 | Where autoscaling is configured, it uses meaningful load metrics (CPU/memory plus queue depth or HTTP queue length), keeps minimum headroom (buffer), and leaves a margin between scale-out and scale-in thresholds to prevent flapping. Max bounds: cost. | autoscale config in scope |
| AZPE-50 | Compute has explicit resource requests and limits (container CPU/memory, runtime heap), so one component can't destabilize others. | container or runtime config in scope |
| AZPE-51 | Text responses are compressed, and HTTP/2 is enabled where clients support it. | HTTP server config in scope |
| AZPE-52 | Static content is served from a CDN or static hosting with caching, not produced by application compute on every request. | app serves static assets |
| AZPE-53 | The processing path has no single-instance bottleneck (one queue consumer or singleton worker for all load) where the work could be partitioned or fanned out. | processing pipelines |
